title: Parsons launches Intelligent Intersections traffic management and signal timing solution
summary: Parsons Corporation has introduced its new Intelligent Intersections solution, a software designed to reduce congestion and improve mobility in cities by using advanced analytics and existing sensor data. This tool automates the retiming of traffic signals, which can reduce congestion by up to 40% and annually decrease GHG emissions by 4.9 million tons and productivity losses by US$27 billion. The solution will be deployed in four US cities including Fort Smith, Arkansas; Austin, Texas; Westminster, Colorado; and Walnut Creek, California, in collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS).

title: Apple begins to sell Sonos as the speaker company accuses Google and Amazon of patent theft
summary: Apple has started selling the Sonos One SL Wireless Speaker online and in its stores. This comes as Sonos has publicly sued Google and accused Amazon of patent theft related to its streaming technology. The Sonos One SL speaker can stream Apple Music via Siri or AirPlay 2.

title: Synchrony Bank Review: High Interest Online Banking
summary: This review covers Synchrony Bank, an online bank offering high-interest deposit products, including savings, money market, and CD accounts, and various credit card options. It highlights the pros and cons of using an online-only bank, such as higher interest rates due to lower overhead but no physical branches. The article also touches on Synchrony's "Loyalty Perks" program and compares it to other online banking alternatives like CIT Bank.

title: Cisco Moves ACI Strategy Forward
summary: Cisco is advancing its hybrid cloud computing strategy with the release of version 5.0 of its Application Centric Infrastructure (ACI), adding support for AWS transit gateways and enhanced integration with Microsoft Azure and Kubernetes. This update aims to provide a centralized view of cloud resources and simplify configurations, offering IT teams networking services equivalent to those historically provided on-premises. The strategy emphasizes hybrid cloud management and automation, making networking services more accessible via APIs and GUIs, and fostering greater collaboration between NetOps and DevOps.

title: FedEx Follows UPS in Raising Delivery Prices Amid Package Surge
summary: FedEx Corp. is increasing its delivery prices for residential and large packages, mirroring an earlier move by UPS, in response to a surge in online orders during the coronavirus lockdown. Effective June 8, new charges will include an extra 30 cents per package for high-volume shippers, 40 cents for "SmartPost" parcels, and $30 for oversized packages. This adjustment reflects the ongoing impact of the pandemic on shipping volumes and operational costs.

title: National Grid Partners Announces New Investments in Two Security Leaders
summary: National Grid Partners announced new investments in two leading online security companies, 1touch.io and RiskIQ, to enhance data security and combat cyber threats. The investments, totaling $14 million and $15 million respectively, highlight National Grid's commitment to delivering a safer energy future. These security solutions are particularly relevant given the increased remote work during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Real Networks' AI Facial Recognition Software IDs Familiar Faces in Streaming Movies and Personal Videos
summary: Real Networks has launched two new AI-powered facial recognition products: StarSearch for identifying actors in streaming movies and TV shows on platforms like Netflix and YouTube, and RealPlayer 20/20 for organizing personal video collections by individuals. These tools aim to address the common user query of identifying faces on screen, leveraging Real's Secure Accurate Facial Recognition (SAFR) software, which boasts high accuracy and low bias. The company envisions expanding the technology to more streaming services and enhancing personal video organization.

title: Fidelity Blue Chip Growth ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the Fidelity Blue Chip Growth ETF (FBCG), an actively-managed, non-transparent fund focusing on large-cap global growth stocks. Established on June 3, 2020, FBCG manages $5393.83 million in assets across 196 holdings, with top investments including NVIDIA, Apple, Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft. The article also provides recent changes in the ETF's shareholdings as of the end of May and June 2022.

title: Amdocs transforms its own culture to help service providers move to the cloud
summary: Amdocs undertook a significant cultural and technological transformation, leveraging TM Forum's Open Digital Framework, to enable its customers to adopt cloud services faster. This involved shifting its portfolio to a cloud-native, microservices-based architecture, upskilling over 10,000 employees in DevOps, and increasing R&D velocity by over 50%. The successful internal transformation is now delivering tangible benefits for Amdocs' customers, such as Sprint, by speeding up time to market for new services and reducing operational costs.

title: US Cloud Data Firm NetApp To Acquire Israel’s Spot.io
summary: US cloud data services company NetApp is set to acquire the US-Israeli company Spot.io for an estimated $450 million. Spot.io helps businesses manage cloud workloads and slash computing costs for clients like Moovit, Ticketmaster, and Wix. This acquisition aims to establish NetApp's leadership in cloud management and infrastructure tools, promising significant cost savings for customers by combining their technologies into an Application Driven Infrastructure.

title: How Snowflake is challenging the cloud-native database giants
summary: This article examines how Snowflake Inc. is competing with major cloud providers like Amazon Web Services, Google, and Microsoft in the cloud-native database market. It analyzes customer spending data from Enterprise Technology Research (ETR) to demonstrate Snowflake's strong spending momentum across all three major clouds and discusses its strategy of being cloud-agnostic and prioritizing engineering investments. The piece concludes that Snowflake's specialized focus and native cloud architecture position it well for continued growth and a successful IPO despite competition from giants with vast R&D budgets.

title: Amazon sues to limit former AWS marketing VP Brian Hall’s new job at Google Cloud
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has filed a lawsuit against Brian Hall, a former VP of product marketing at Amazon Web Services Inc., to prevent him from taking a new role at Google Cloud due to a noncompete agreement. The lawsuit claims Hall's move risks exposing "valuable competitive information" related to Amazon's cloud product roadmap and strategy. Hall's lawyers argue the noncompete clause is overbroad and unenforceable, citing prior assurances from an AWS executive and Amazon's non-enforcement against another executive who joined a rival.

title: In Retreat, Wall Street Pulls Back From Rally (Published 2020)
summary: Wall Street experienced a retreat after a recent rally, with stocks falling on Tuesday despite the S&P 500 erasing its yearly losses on Monday. Concerns about a potential second wave of the coronavirus outbreak are affecting investor sentiment, even as global economies show signs of recovery and central banks provide support. This article summarizes key market movements and includes snapshots of news from companies like Chesapeake Energy and AMC.

title: Morgan Stanley's Gorman 'thrilled' with ETrade purchase
summary: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman expresses immense satisfaction with the acquisition of ETrade, highlighting the online trading firm's technology, digital banking capabilities, and management team. He plans to retain the ETrade brand, possibly as "ETrade powered by Morgan Stanley," recognizing its value to clients. Gorman believes the deal expands Morgan Stanley's online platform, diversifies the company, and strengthens its digital offerings, particularly appealing to a younger demographic.

title: Rackspace rebrands (again) and repositions for digital transformation
summary: Rackspace has rebranded itself as Rackspace Technology and repositioned its strategy to focus on end-to-end technology solutions across four key areas, including cloud optimization, security, cloud-native enablement, and data modernization. This move follows a series of acquisitions and strategic partnerships, as the company prepares for a potential new initial public offering. The company aims to tackle the entire technology transformation lifecycle for its customers.

title: Hedge Fund and Insider Trading News: Mitch Rubin, Stanley Druckenmiller, Lynwood Capital Management, Bow Street LLC, Ecolab Inc. (ECL), Ball Corporation (BLL), and More
summary: This article compiles various hedge fund and insider trading news, featuring fund managers like Mitch Rubin and Stanley Druckenmiller, and discussing their investment strategies and portfolio performance. It also covers several significant insider transactions in companies such as Ecolab Inc. (ECL) and Ball Corporation (BLL), and reports on the growth of crypto hedge funds in Gibraltar, new healthcare startups, and a regulatory charge against a penny stock trader for a manipulative scheme.

title: Here’s what that Capital One court decision means for corporate cybersecurity
summary: A recent court decision regarding Capital One's data breach mandated the bank to reveal a third-party incident response report, challenging the traditional attorney-client privilege over such documents. This ruling could significantly impact how companies contract cybersecurity firms and manage incident response, potentially making breach details public. Legal experts suggest this decision will prompt corporations to re-evaluate their agreements with security vendors to preserve legal protections.

title: Walmart buys tech from Carezone to help people manage their prescriptions
summary: Walmart has acquired technology and intellectual property from the start-up CareZone to enhance its health and wellness services, particularly in medication management. This acquisition includes bringing CareZone's engineering and product teams into Walmart, but Walmart is not purchasing CareZone's pharmacy business. The move is seen as a strategic step for Walmart to compete with Amazon in the pharmacy space and make healthcare more accessible and affordable for its customers.

title: Fact Check: Do Cruise Lines Pay US Taxes?
summary: This article clarifies whether cruise lines pay U.S. taxes, explaining that while they generally avoid federal income taxes due to international shipping agreements, they pay other significant taxes and fees. It details the tax amounts paid by major cruise corporations like Carnival Corp., Royal Caribbean Cruises, Ltd., and Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings, highlighting the relatively low effective tax rates compared to typical corporate rates. The article also debunks the myth that cruise lines sought a U.S. government bailout and notes that many profitable Fortune 500 companies also avoid federal taxes.

title: Oracle expects flat sales on fewer corporate software deals
summary: Oracle Corp. projects flat revenue in the current quarter due to delayed software purchases by corporate clients amid the coronavirus pandemic. The company, the world's second-biggest software-maker, reported a 6.3% decline in fiscal fourth-quarter revenue, missing analyst estimates. Oracle is struggling to shift existing database customers to cloud-based offerings and compete with Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp.

title: Target permanently raises starting hourly pay to $15
summary: Target Corp. announced it is permanently increasing starting hourly wages for its workers to $15 beginning July 5, several months ahead of its original 2020 goal. This move comes after a temporary $2 wage bump for workers due to increased demand during the pandemic. The company will invest nearly $1 billion more this year in its workers, including a $200 bonus and extended COVID-19 benefits.

title: Salesforce Launches Government Cloud Plus, Achieves FedRAMP Provisional Authority to Operate at the High Security Impact Level
summary: Salesforce has launched Government Cloud Plus, a dedicated cloud instance for U.S. federal, state, and local government customers, achieving FedRAMP Provisional Authority to Operate (P-ATO) at the High Security Impact Level. This new offering provides enhanced security and compliance, running on AWS GovCloud (US), to help government agencies modernize their systems and deliver services more efficiently amidst evolving demands. Government Cloud Plus aims to reduce IT costs and complexity while offering the full power of Salesforce's Customer 360 CRM platform tailored for secure government use cases.

title: Amazon to hire 3,000 people in South Africa for customer service roles
summary: Amazon.com Inc. announced it will hire 3,000 people in South Africa this year for customer service roles, supporting customers in North America and Europe. These work-from-home positions, ranging from customer service associates to technical experts, will increase Amazon's permanent workforce in South Africa to 7,000. This expansion highlights South Africa's value proposition for global companies, following Amazon Web Services' launch of its first data center in Cape Town in April.

title: This NAACP-backed ETF will help you invest in companies that care about equality
summary: The Impact Shares NAACP Minority Empowerment ETF (NACP) allows investors to support companies committed to diversity and racial equality. Developed in partnership with the NAACP and Impact Shares, the ETF screens companies based on their practices in hiring, pay, promotion, and supply chains, with net proceeds going to the NAACP for social advocacy. With over $4 million in net assets and holdings in major companies like Amazon and Microsoft, the fund aims to achieve "social alpha" by investing in corporate leaders in social justice.

title: Montclair Woman Makes History At American Express, Joins Top Team
summary: Montclair resident Glenda McNeal has been appointed to American Express' executive committee, making her the first African American woman to hold such a position. Having served over 30 years with the company, McNeal’s elevation comes as a significant milestone, strengthening the committee's female representation. She will continue to lead strategic partnerships with major e-commerce, travel, technology, and retail companies.

title: Amazon Facing Class Action Alleging PFAS in Disposable Plates
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is facing a proposed class action lawsuit alleging that its disposable plates and bowls, advertised as compostable, actually contain PFAS "forever" chemicals. The plaintiff claims he purchased these products, which cost more than non-compostable alternatives, believing they were environmentally friendly and would not have bought them if he knew they contained PFAS. The lawsuit highlights concerns about the contamination of soil by these chemicals.

title: After 15 Years, Apple Prepares to Break Up With Intel (Published 2020)
summary: Apple is preparing to end its 15-year partnership with Intel, with plans to replace Intel processors in Macs with self-designed chips. This move, expected to be announced soon, signifies Apple's growing independence and determination to control its product manufacturing, a trend seen among other major tech companies like Facebook, Amazon, and Google. The new Mac chips are anticipated to arrive next year and will likely be manufactured by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing.

title: American Express Names Glenda McNeal as the First Black Woman on its Executive Committee
summary: Glenda McNeal has been appointed as the first Black woman to join the Executive Committee at American Express, where she will bring her extensive expertise in strategic partnerships to help navigate global economic challenges. McNeal, who has a storied three-decade career, has overseen relationships with major Amex partners and serves on several boards. Her appointment also marks a record number of seven women on the committee, with leadership praising her diverse perspectives.

title: Sheltering-In and Shopping Online
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly accelerated the shift to online shopping, especially for softline retail sales, with e-commerce expected to account for 32% of softline sales in 2020. This shift is predicted to negatively impact brick-and-mortar retail margins due to cannibalized store sales and fixed costs, while benefiting e-commerce giants and brands with strong direct-to-consumer businesses. Morgan Stanley Research has raised its U.S. e-commerce estimates for both 2020 and 2021, emphasizing the long-term changes in consumer behavior.

title: Kroger CEO: Company's heavy tech investments vindicated. 'We made the right decision.'
summary: Kroger CEO Rodney McMullen stated that the company's significant investments in digital shopping initiatives have positioned it for future growth and allowed it to meet the increased demand during the coronavirus pandemic. He highlighted the vindication of their business model transformation and the expansion of digital capabilities, including new robotic delivery hubs. The company also announced a 12.5% increase in its quarterly dividend.

title: LATEST TECH NEWS: Verizon joins others to boycott Facebook. 4 other things and a trivia you need to know today, June 26, 2020
summary: This article covers five key tech news stories from June 26, 2020, including Verizon joining the boycott against Facebook due to hate speech concerns, Egyptian edtech OTO Courses securing new investment, Waymo and Volvo partnering on electric robotaxis, the opening of applications for the AppsAfrica Innovation Awards 2020, and Amazon's reported acquisition of self-driving startup Zoox for over $1 billion. It also includes a tech trivia question and answer about the beginning of computer engineering.

title: 3 ETFs With Rising Profit Forecasts
summary: Despite a challenging economic environment and a potential second wave of COVID-19, some ETFs are showing rising earnings forecasts. The ETF Research Center identified three such funds: the Brand Value ETF (BVAL), the Roundhill BITKRAFT Esports & Digital Entertainment ETF (NERD), and the VanEck Vectors Environmental Services ETF (EVX), which are seeing positive revisions in their component companies' 2020 earnings estimates, indicating resilience and growth potential in their respective sectors.

title: A Thank You bonus for Amazon front-line employees and partners
summary: Amazon announced a one-time "Thank You" bonus totaling over $500 million for its front-line employees and partners in recognition of their efforts during June 2020. The bonus amounts vary based on employment status and role, with full-time Amazon and Whole Foods Market employees, and Delivery Service Partner drivers receiving $500, and front-line leaders receiving $1,000, among others. Dave Clark, SVP WW Operations, expressed gratitude for their commitment to customers.

title: Special Feature: YouTube’s Evolution in the OTT Streaming Landscape...
summary: This article by Comscore and YouTube examines YouTube's significant growth within the evolving OTT streaming landscape, highlighting its increased reach in ad-supported households and substantial growth in CTV watch time. It also details how YouTube's unique user-generated content and extensive library are providing new opportunities for advertisers to target diverse audiences. The piece further explores emerging content consumption trends on the platform, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Santander appoints three leading technologists to support its strategy and digital transformation
summary: Santander has appointed R. Martin Chávez, Sebastian Gunningham, and Francisco D’Souza to key roles to bolster its digital transformation. Chávez will join the board as an independent director, Gunningham will chair Santander Consumer Finance and become vice chairman of Openbank, and D’Souza will be a strategic advisor for Santander Global Platform. These appointments aim to leverage their extensive technology and financial sector experience to drive Santander's digital strategy.

title: Target to open two-level store in former Boston Store space at Bayshore
summary: Target is scheduled to open a new two-level store in the former Boston Store space at the Bayshore shopping center in Glendale. This announcement was made by mall manager Cypress Equities on June 30, 2020. This development implies a significant revitalization for the Bayshore shopping center.
